title: Policy and government debt
summary: [[monetary-policy|Monetary policy]] (the central bank's rates) and [[fiscal-policy|fiscal policy]] (the government's spending and taxes) both affect growth and inflation. Deficits add to [[government-debt]], and higher rates make that debt more costly.
unreliableWhen: When the two policies pull in opposite directions, when the reaction depends on how lenders feel about the debt that day, or when one debt figure is treated as a fixed danger line. There is no single level at which debt becomes a problem.
goodExample: A learner reads fictional Westmark's bigger-than-expected deficit and lists two chains: the central bank keeping rates high (WMK up) and debt worries (WMK down). They plan for either.
badExample: A learner assumes a bigger deficit must sink the currency, ignoring that the central bank may respond with higher rates.
